First, let's recall the following result:

$$
\int {b}^{\,px+q}\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{p\operatorname{ln}⁡(b)}{b}^{\,px+q}+C
$$

We proceed by setting the lower bound equal to some parameter $a,$ integrating as usual, and then taking the limit as $a\to -\infty .$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-\infty }^{2}{2}^{3x/2}\,\text{d}x & ={lim}_{a\to -\infty }{\int }_{a}^{2}{2}^{3x/2}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={lim}_{a\to -\infty }{[\frac{{2}^{3x/2}}{3\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)/2}]}_{a}^{2} \\  & =\frac{2}{3\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)}\cdot {lim}_{a\to -\infty }{[{2}^{3x/2}]}_{a}^{2} \\  & =\frac{2}{3\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)}\cdot {lim}_{a\to -\infty }(8-{2}^{3a/2}) \\  & =\frac{2}{3\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)}\cdot (8-{lim}_{a\to -\infty }{2}^{3a/2})\end{aligned}
$$

Now, recall the end behavior of the function $y={2}^{3x/2}$ shown in the graph below:

- ${lim}_{x\to -\infty }{2}^{3x/2}=0$

- ${lim}_{x\to \infty }{2}^{3x/2}=\infty $

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14260591/assets/be9ec5171eb254ce770b8ad91c72cc6bd906359c7bf4c3d52a4617a9c87af983.png)

Using this to evaluate our integral, we conclude that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-\infty }^{2}{2}^{3x/2}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{2}{3\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)}\cdot (8-{lim}_{a\to -\infty }{2}^{3a/2}) \\  & =\frac{2}{3\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)}\cdot (8-0) \\  & =\frac{16}{3\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)}.\end{aligned}
$$
